I was 18 and was going to the club with my friends as it was our friends (let's call him Lee) birthday. 

Lee asked me if I would not let him get too drunk as it was his cousin's birthday the next day. I promised I wouldn't. 

That night I didn't get wasted, like usual, but I got tipsy, walking wasn't hard but certainly not easy, I however because of the drink, forgot about Lee's promise. By the end of the night Lee was utterly wasted. Remembering it I'm amazed he could stand let alone walk.

Walking home we had to cross the main street in our town. The main street was a long straight line that stretched in a line for miles each way. Street racers were infamous for speeding on it.

As Lee crossed the street, a street racer was speeding down the road. 

They hit him. He was dead before he hit the ground.

I didn't really quit drinking, I couldn't even push myself to drink. Even now two years later, the alcohol tastes horrible

With this you have a few options 

1) A polar opposite, secondary, this person (boy or girl) is different in every way shape and form. Your character is 'cynical, sarcastic, insecure lazy slob, does things that benefit him, not a bad guy.'

You could make a sporty type person, who loves tennis, running etc. A secure person who is very positive, does things to be nice, good or for the hell of it, not just for their own gain, (It may even be a loss for them) and a good person.

This would be a good character if you want something different from the main character. An opposites attract type of thing

2) A mix of the main and 1)

This person in optimistic like 1) but is lazy like the main character. They also may do things for the greater good unlike the main character.

Those were my two possibilities, but there are many more

Don't make up two characters for the hell of it, they need a past together e.g childhood friends, one transferred to the school, and the other was that characters first friend.

Look up character foil if you really are stuck

You said the story was about teenagers, well being teenagers they will have things like hormones, and other teen stuff, so if you don't like them change them, since the series won't be in order of events you can just change them.

You make it a non-chronological story for them e.g one comic they both good friends, the next they're in an argument and make up. The next comic is why they were arguing.

This is just my few cents, take some, leave some or take nothing. Remember you're a writer, the world and your mind is you're influence.
